mainTopic: How the year of an אתרוג and other tree fruit is set for מעשר and שביעית, and ריש לקיש's challenge to רבי יוחנן about carobs
overview: The גמרא fills in missing words in a ברייתא. אבטולמוס said an אתרוג follows its picking for מעשר but its forming (חנטה) for שביעית, and the חכמים at אושא voted that picking decides both. רבי יוחנן and ריש לקיש rule that a sixth-year אתרוג that went into שביעית stays sixth-year fruit, and רבין adds that this is true even if it grew from olive-size to loaf-size. A ברייתא then teaches that ט״ו בשבט divides the years for tree fruit, and רבי נחמיה limits this to trees that give two crops a year. For one-crop trees like carobs, he says picking decides, and רבי יוחנן reports that people followed רבי נחמיה for carobs. ריש לקיש challenges this from white figs, and רבי יוחנן stays silent. רבי אבא הכהן and רבי יוסי הכהן discuss which answers רבי יוחנן could have given; the first two are rejected, and the third is not. So רבי אבא הכהן wonders whether רבי יוחנן's silence meant he accepted the question or thought it did not deserve an answer.

steps.title: The ברייתא is missing words: אבטולמוס splits מעשר and שביעית
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers the earlier problem by saying the ברייתא is missing words. אבטולמוס really said: an אתרוג follows its picking for מעשר, but its forming for שביעית.
steps.simpleTranslation: Words are missing from the ברייתא, and this is what it teaches: an אתרוג follows its picking for מעשר, and follows its forming for שביעית.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא solves the earlier difficulty by filling in missing words in the ברייתא. The fuller text shows what אבטולמוס actually said.
steps.deeperAnalysis: As it stood, the ברייתא made it look like אבטולמוס and the vote at אושא said the same thing, so the vote seemed to add nothing. With the missing words restored, אבטולמוס uses two different rules: picking for מעשר and forming (חנטה) for שביעית. Now the vote at אושא is a real change.

keyTerms.meaning: Words are missing from the text
And this is what it teaches
The early forming of the fruit
The seventh year of the cycle, the שמיטה year

steps.confusionAlert: Don't think אבטולמוס held one rule for everything. For him, an אתרוג follows two different dates: picking for מעשר and forming for שביעית.

phrases.english: It is missing words
and this is what it teaches:
An etrog follows its picking for tithes
and follows its forming for the Sabbatical Year.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the difficulty raised just before this section about the ברייתא's wording.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Filling in missing words in the text
steps.terutzHavaAmina: אבטולמוס seemed to say picking decides everything, the same as the vote at אושא.
steps.terutzMaskana: אבטולמוס said picking for מעשר but forming for שביעית, so the vote at אושא changed the rule for שביעית.

steps.title: The vote at אושא: picking decides both
steps.stepSummary: The חכמים at אושא voted that an אתרוג follows its picking for both מעשר and שביעית.
steps.simpleTranslation: And our Rabbis voted at אושא: an אתרוג follows its picking, both for מעשר and for שביעית.
steps.whatsHappening: The fixed ברייתא continues with the vote of the חכמים at אושא. They ruled that picking decides the year for both מעשר and שביעית.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This disagrees with אבטולמוס only about שביעית. He followed forming for שביעית, while אושא follows picking for both. So with one rule, the year of picking settles everything.

keyTerms.meaning: אושא, the town where the חכמים met and voted

steps.whatToRemember: The final ruling from אושא: an אתרוג follows its picking for both מעשר and שביעית.

phrases.english: And our Rabbis voted in Usha:
it follows its picking,
both for tithes and for the Sabbatical Year.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: The second half of the fixed ברייתא, which disagrees with אבטולמוס about שביעית.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: An אתרוג follows the time of its picking for both מעשר and שביעית.

steps.title: A sixth-year אתרוג picked in שביעית stays sixth-year fruit
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן and ריש לקיש both rule that an אתרוג that formed in the sixth year and went into שביעית is always treated as sixth-year fruit.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was said: רבי יוחנן and ריש לקיש both say: an אתרוג of the sixth year that went into שביעית is always sixth-year fruit.
steps.whatsHappening: Two אמוראים give a ruling about an אתרוג that started growing in the sixth year and was still on the tree when שביעית began. They say it counts as sixth-year fruit.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This seems to follow the year the fruit started, not the year it was picked, which is different from the vote at אושא. The ruling is simple and stated without exceptions: such an אתרוג always counts as sixth-year fruit.

phrases.english: It was stated: Rabbi Yoḥanan and Reish Lakish
both say:
An etrog of the sixth year
that entered into the Sabbatical Year —
is always sixth-year produce.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִיתְּמַר, רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן וְרֵישׁ לָקִישׁ אָמְרִי תַּרְוַיְיהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the תנאים's argument to a ruling of the אמוראים on the same topic.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A sixth-year אתרוג that went into שביעית is treated as sixth-year fruit.

steps.title: רבין: even if it grew from olive-size to loaf-size
steps.stepSummary: רבין reports from רבי יוחנן that the rule holds even if the אתרוג was only olive-size when שביעית began and grew to loaf-size during it. You are still liable for eating it as טבל.
steps.simpleTranslation: When רבין came, he said in the name of רבי יוחנן: a sixth-year אתרוג that went into שביעית, even if it was the size of an olive and became the size of a loaf, people are liable for it because of טבל.
steps.whatsHappening: רבין brings a sharper version of רבי יוחנן's rule. Even if most of the fruit's growth happened in שביעית, it still counts as sixth-year fruit that needs מעשר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: You might think that if most of the growth happened in שביעית, it should count as שביעית fruit, which has no מעשר. רבי יוחנן says no: it is sixth-year fruit, so it needs מעשר. Anyone who eats it without taking מעשר is liable for eating טבל.

keyTerms.meaning: When רבין came (from ארץ ישראל to בבל)
Produce from which מעשר has not yet been taken; forbidden to eat

steps.whyThisMatters: It shows how strongly this ruling holds: no amount of growth in שביעית changes the fruit's status.

phrases.aramaic: כִּי אֲתָא רָבִין אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן:
phrases.english: When Ravin came, he said that Rabbi Yoḥanan said:
A sixth-year etrog that entered into the Sabbatical Year,
even if it was olive-size and became loaf-size —
one is liable for it because of untithed produce.

steps.triggerLanguage: כִּי אֲתָא רָבִין אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Strengthens the rule from step 3 by applying it to an extreme case.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Even an אתרוג that did most of its growing in שביעית is sixth-year fruit and must have מעשר taken.

steps.title: ט״ו בשבט divides the years for tree fruit
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא teaches that fruit that formed before ט״ו בשבט is tithed with the previous year, and fruit that formed after it is tithed with the coming year.
steps.simpleTranslation: The חכמים taught: a tree whose fruits formed before ט״ו בשבט is tithed for the past year; after ט״ו בשבט, it is tithed for the coming year.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new ברייתא about how ט״ו בשבט works as the dividing line between years for tree fruit.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The deciding moment is when the fruit forms (חנטה), not when it is picked. Fruit that formed before ט״ו בשבט belongs to the old year, and fruit that formed after it belongs to the new year. This matters because fruit from different years cannot be tithed together.

keyTerms.meaning: They formed (the fruit began to form)

phrases.english: The Sages taught:
A tree whose fruits formed
before the fifteenth of Shevat —
is tithed for the year that passed,
after the fifteenth of Shevat —
it is tithed for the coming year.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: אִילָן שֶׁחָנְטוּ פֵּירוֹתָיו קוֹדֶם חֲמִשָּׁה עָשָׂר בִּשְׁבָט
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic: the general rule of ט״ו בשבט for trees.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: For tree fruit, forming before or after ט״ו בשבט decides which year it is tithed with.

steps.title: רבי נחמיה limits the rule to trees with two crops
steps.stepSummary: רבי נחמיה says the ט״ו בשבט rule applies to a tree that produces two 'broods' in a year.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי נחמיה said: When does this apply? To a tree that makes two broods in a year.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי נחמיה narrows the ברייתא's rule to one kind of tree.
steps.deeperAnalysis: He does not cancel the ט״ו בשבט rule. He tells us which trees it is talking about: trees that give fruit twice a year. His word 'בריכות' will be questioned in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: When does this apply? (introduces a limit on a rule)
Broods (a word normally used for animals giving birth)

phrases.english: Rabbi Neḥemya said:
In what case is this said —
with a tree that produces
two broods in a year.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי נְחֶמְיָה: בַּמֶּה דְּבָרִים אֲמוּרִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Puts a limit on the ברייתא's ט״ו בשבט rule.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The ט״ו בשבט rule is said about a tree that bears fruit twice a year.

steps.title: Can a tree really have 'broods'?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא stops to question רבי נחמיה's word: trees don't produce 'broods.'
steps.simpleTranslation: Two broods, can you really think so?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pauses to question the wording. This sets up the correction in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'Broods' describes animals giving birth, not trees growing fruit. So the wording can't be meant literally.

keyTerms.meaning: Can it enter your mind? (this can't be right)

phrases.english: Two broods — can that enter your mind?
phrases.notes: Animals have broods, trees don't, so the גמרא can't take the word literally.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions the word רבי נחמיה used in step 6.
steps.kashyaTarget: The word 'בריכות' in רבי נחמיה's statement
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Trees do not literally produce broods the way animals do.

steps.title: Read it as 'like two broods'
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא fixes the reading: 'like two broods,' meaning two crops, like two batches of young.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers its question by adjusting the wording so it is a comparison.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With the word 'like' added, רבי נחמיה is not saying trees literally have broods. He is comparing a tree's two crops in a year to two batches of young. The meaning of his rule stays the same.

phrases.english: Rather, say:
like two broods.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the wording question from step 7.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא literally says a tree makes broods.
steps.terutzMaskana: It means two crops in a year, which are like two broods.

steps.title: Trees with one crop a year go with the coming year
steps.stepSummary: רבי נחמיה's ברייתא continues: trees that give one crop a year, like palms, olives and carobs, are tithed with the coming year even if their fruit formed before ט״ו בשבט.
steps.simpleTranslation: But a tree that gives only one crop a year, like palm trees, olive trees and carob trees, is tithed with the next year, even if its fruit formed before ט״ו בשבט.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא of רבי נחמיה finishes its rule. It now tells us what happens to trees that give only one crop a year.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For two-crop trees, ט״ו בשבט and the time the fruit formed (חנטה) decide the year. For one-crop trees, רבי נחמיה says the formation date does not decide. The fruit goes with the coming year, because what counts is when it is picked.

keyTerms.meaning: A 'brood', meaning one crop or batch of fruit
The fruit formed (the early stage of fruit growth)

steps.whyThisMatters: This line sets up everything that follows. רבי יוחנן's report and ריש לקיש's challenge both depend on רבי נחמיה's rule for one-crop trees.

phrases.english: But a tree that produces one brood (one crop),
for example, palm trees, olive trees and carob trees,
even though their fruit formed
before the fifteenth of שבט,
they are tithed with the coming year.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes רבי נחמיה's ברייתא, which was interrupted by the wording question in steps 7-8.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רבי נחמיה, one-crop trees are tithed by the year of picking, even if the fruit formed before ט״ו בשבט.

steps.title: People followed רבי נחמיה for carobs
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן reports that the common practice with carobs followed רבי נחמיה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן said: The people's practice with carobs was to follow רבי נחמיה.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן tells us how people actually behaved. For carobs, they followed רבי נחמיה's view.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Carobs are one of the one-crop trees named in the ברייתא. So people tithed carobs by when they were picked, not by when the fruit formed.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yochanan said:
The people were accustomed to act with carobs like Rabbi Nechemya.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Reports how רבי נחמיה's rule from step 9 was followed in practice.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: In practice, carobs were tithed by the year of picking, as רבי נחמיה says.

steps.title: ריש לקיש challenges from white figs
steps.stepSummary: ריש לקיש brings a משנה about white figs that seems to go by when the fruit formed, against רבי נחמיה's approach.
steps.simpleTranslation: ריש לקיש challenged רבי יוחנן: White figs have their שביעית year in the second year, because their fruit takes three years to grow!
steps.whatsHappening: ריש לקיש attacks רבי יוחנן's statement. He brings a משנה that seems to say the opposite.
steps.deeperAnalysis: White fig fruit takes three years to ripen. Fruit picked in the second year of the cycle had already formed during שביעית. The משנה still treats it as שביעית fruit, so it goes by when the fruit formed, not when it was picked. That clashes with following רבי נחמיה.

keyTerms.meaning: White figs, a kind of fig that takes years to ripen
The seventh year, when special laws apply to produce

steps.confusionAlert: 'Their שביעית is the second year' does not mean they have a different cycle. It means the שביעית laws apply to their fruit picked in year two, because that fruit formed during year seven.

phrases.english: Reish Lakish raised an objection to Rabbi Yochanan:
White figs:
their seventh year is the second year,
phrases.notes: The שביעית laws apply to their fruit picked in the year after שביעית.

phrases.english: because they produce fruit over three years!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רבי יוחנן's report in step 10.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יוחנן's statement that people followed רבי נחמיה, which goes by picking time.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The white-fig משנה treats fruit by when it formed (חנטה), not when it was picked. That contradicts following the picking time.

steps.title: The answer רבי יוחנן could have given
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן was silent. רבי אבא הכהן says he could have answered that the משנה follows the רבנן, while he was speaking about רבי נחמיה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן was silent. רבי אבא הכהן said to רבי יוסי הכהן: Why was he silent? He should have said: I am telling you רבי נחמיה's view, and you answer me with the view of the רבנן?!
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן did not answer the challenge. A later scholar points out an easy answer he could have given.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The white-fig משנה follows the רבנן, who go by when the fruit formed. רבי יוחנן only said people followed רבי נחמיה, who disagrees with the רבנן. A source from the other side of a debate cannot disprove what one side holds.

phrases.english: He was silent.
phrases.notes: This is רבי יוחנן. He gave no answer to ריש לקיש.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַבִּי אַבָּא הַכֹּהֵן לְרַבִּי יוֹסֵי הַכֹּהֵן:
phrases.english: Rabbi Abba the priest said to Rabbi Yosei the priest:
Why was he silent?
Let him say to him:
I am telling you Rabbi Nechemya's view,
and you tell me the Rabbis' view?!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers ריש לקיש's challenge from step 11 for רבי יוחנן.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Assigning the source to the other side of a debate (the רבנן, not רבי נחמיה).
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The white-fig משנה seemed to disprove the practice of following רבי נחמיה.
steps.terutzMaskana: Suggested answer: the משנה follows the רבנן, while רבי יוחנן reported practice like רבי נחמיה. Step 13 shows why רבי יוחנן could not have used this answer.

steps.title: Why the 'משנה follows the רבנן' answer would not work
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן could not answer that the משנה follows the רבנן. ריש לקיש would have replied: you leave the majority and act like the lone opinion of רבי נחמיה?
steps.simpleTranslation: Because ריש לקיש would have said to him: You leave the רבנן and act like רבי נחמיה?!
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוסי הכהן answers רבי אבא הכהן and explains why רבי יוחנן did not give the answer suggested in step 12. That answer would only have opened him to a sharper attack.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Saying 'the משנה follows the רבנן' admits that the common practice follows a single dissenting opinion against the majority. ריש לקיש could then ask why anyone should practice that way. So the answer would not really have helped.

phrases.english: Because he would have said to him:
phrases.notes: This explains why רבי יוחנן couldn't give that answer. ריש לקיש would have come right back at him.

phrases.english: You leave the רבנן
and act like רבי נחמיה?!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the answer רבי אבא הכהן suggested in step 12.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The suggested answer that the white figs משנה follows the רבנן.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: It admits that the practice follows a lone opinion against the majority, which ריש לקיש would attack.

steps.title: Suggestion: רבי יוחנן was only describing custom
steps.stepSummary: רבי אבא הכהן suggests another answer: רבי יוחנן was only reporting what people did, and ריש לקיש is talking about a prohibition.
steps.simpleTranslation: But let him say to him: I am telling you what people practiced, and you tell me about a prohibition?!
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אבא הכהן suggests a second answer רבי יוחנן could have given: he only reported a custom, not a ruling.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוחנן's statement in step 10 used the word נהגו, 'they practiced.' This suggestion says a report of custom cannot be refuted by a source about what is forbidden.

keyTerms.meaning: but let him say to him (why didn't he answer this way?)

phrases.english: But let him say to him:
I am telling you "they practiced,"
phrases.notes: This points back to step 10, where רבי יוחנן said people 'practiced' like רבי נחמיה.

phrases.english: and you tell me about a prohibition?!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the first answer was rejected, a second possible answer is offered.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If a simple answer was available, why didn't רבי יוחנן use it?

steps.title: Custom does not override a prohibition
steps.stepSummary: That answer fails too. Where something is forbidden, we do not let people keep a custom just because they are used to it.
steps.simpleTranslation: Because he would have said to him: Where there is a prohibition, do we leave people alone just because that is their practice?!
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוסי הכהן rejects the second suggested answer, because ריש לקיש would have had a reply.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A custom cannot permit something that is actually forbidden. If ריש לקיש's source shows a prohibition, the custom would have to be stopped, not just reported.

phrases.english: Because he would have said to him:
Where there is a prohibition,
because they practiced so, do we leave them alone?!

steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The idea that רבי יוחנן was only reporting custom.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: A custom cannot stand where there is a real prohibition.

steps.title: Suggestion: carob tithes are rabbinic, while שביעית is from the Torah
steps.stepSummary: A third answer: רבי יוחנן was talking about מעשר on carobs, which is only rabbinic. The white figs case is about שביעית, which is from the Torah. No rejection follows.
steps.simpleTranslation: But let him say to him: When I speak to you, it is about carob tithes, which are rabbinic, and you tell me about שביעית, which is from the Torah?!
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אבא הכהן suggests a third answer רבי יוחנן could have given. This time no rejection follows.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The white figs case concerns שביעית, a Torah law. Carob tithes are only rabbinic. A stricter standard in a Torah law does not prove anything about a rabbinic tithe, so ריש לקיש's challenge falls away. Since this answer is not refuted, רבי יוחנן's silence still needs an explanation.
steps.confusionAlert: This is not a ruling that carob tithes don't matter. The point is only that a rabbinic rule can be more lenient than a Torah rule, so one cannot prove the other.

phrases.english: But let him say to him:
When I speak to you,
it is about carob tithes, which are rabbinic,
and you tell me
about שביעית, which is from the Torah?!
phrases.notes: ריש לקיש's white figs משנה from step 11 is about the שמיטה year.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְלֵימָא לֵיהּ: כִּי אָמֵינָא לָךְ אֲנָא מַעֲשֵׂר חָרוּבִין דְּרַבָּנַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the second answer was rejected, a third and stronger answer is offered.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A good answer existed, because Torah law and rabbinic law are different, so his silence is hard to understand.
steps.whyThisMatters: This answer is never rejected. That is what pushes the גמרא to rethink the question in the next steps.

steps.title: רבי אבא הכהן wonders whether ריש לקיש really asked this
steps.stepSummary: Because there is such a clear answer, רבי אבא הכהן says: I wonder whether ריש לקיש really raised this objection.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, רבי אבא הכהן said: I wonder whether ריש לקיש raised this objection.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אבא הכהן changes his approach. Instead of asking why רבי יוחנן did not answer, he questions whether the objection was ever asked. This line sets up the next move.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The objection seems so easy to answer that he finds it hard to believe ריש לקיש actually raised it.

phrases.english: Rather, רבי אבא הכהן said:
I wonder whether ריש לקיש raised
phrases.notes: Here תשובה means a challenge, not an answer.

phrases.english: this objection.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא אָמַר רַבִּי אַבָּא הַכֹּהֵן: תְּמֵיהַנִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Since step 16 is not refuted, the question is reframed.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Given how easy the answer is, it is surprising that ריש לקיש raised this objection.

steps.title: But he clearly did ask it
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא objects: how can you wonder whether he asked it? The story says he did.
steps.simpleTranslation: Whether he raised it? But he did raise it!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רבי אבא הכהן's wording, because the story clearly reports that ריש לקיש asked.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There is no doubt about whether the question was asked. So רבי אבא הכהן's doubt must be about something else.

keyTerms.meaning: but he did raise it as a challenge

phrases.english: Whether he raised it?
But he did raise it!
phrases.notes: This points back to step 11, where ריש לקיש actually brought the white figs משנה.

steps.kashyaTarget: רבי אבא הכהן's statement in step 17
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The story plainly says ריש לקיש asked, so 'I wonder whether he asked' makes no sense.

steps.title: The real doubt: did רבי יוחנן accept the question?
steps.stepSummary: The wording is fixed: רבי אבא הכהן wondered whether רבי יוחנן accepted the question or did not accept it.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, say: I wonder whether רבי יוחנן accepted it, or did not accept it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא corrects רבי אבא הכהן's words. His doubt is about why רבי יוחנן was silent.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Silence can mean two things. Either רבי יוחנן agreed the question was strong and had no answer, or he rejected it and felt it did not deserve a reply. Because a good answer exists (step 16), the second reading is possible, so the doubt is left open.
steps.whatToRemember: ריש לקיש's white figs challenge has a good answer: carob tithes are rabbinic, while שביעית is from the Torah. So רבי יוחנן's silence may not mean he was defeated. It is left open whether he accepted the question or simply ignored it.

phrases.english: Rather, say:
whether רבי יוחנן accepted it,
or did not accept it.
phrases.notes: Maybe רבי יוחנן stayed quiet because he didn't think the question was worth answering.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא אֵימָא: אִם קִיבְּלָהּ רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 18 by rereading רבי אבא הכהן's statement.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Rereading the wording of the statement
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי אבא הכהן doubted whether ריש לקיש asked the question at all.
steps.terutzMaskana: He doubted whether רבי יוחנן's silence meant he accepted the question or rejected it.
